extracted.intended_audience: public relations and marketing professionals, brand communicators, PR teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating, earning, and measuring earned media (organic third-party coverage, mentions, reviews, influencer pickup) to build brand awareness, trust, and business results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of earned media
rubrics_metrics.description: Earned media is the visibility your business 'earns' from organic sources; it comes from third-party sources rather than being created directly by your brand or paid for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast earned media with paid media (advertising with guaranteed placement) and owned media (channels you control like your website/blog). Shared media includes your social posts, but organic mentions/shares from others are earned media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned media must be third-party and organic
rubrics_metrics.description: By definition, earned media isn’t created directly by your brand or paid for — you 'earn' it through reputation, word-of-mouth, and public relations efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because it comes from third parties it carries unique benefits such as greater credibility and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility and trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Earned media builds credibility because it originates from third-party sources rather than directly from your brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use earned coverage to foster trust: surveys show customers reduce purchases when trust is lost and remain loyal to trusted companies. Leverage third-party endorsements like reviews, press mentions, and influencer mentions to boost perceived credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased reach and brand awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Earned media can expand who sees your brand and introduce you to new demographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-profile organic mentions (e.g., celebrities wearing or name-dropping a brand) and press coverage can help reach younger or otherwise hard-to-reach audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer loyalty through authentic connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentic connections created via earned media can encourage repeat purchases and word-of-mouth recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on storytelling and values that resonate (sustainability, ethics) to build long-term loyalty rather than short-term sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost considerations and investment
rubrics_metrics.description: Earned media is typically more affordable than paid media but is not always free — it can require teams, software, and product placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for earned media management (PR teams and specialized software) and recognize upfront investments may be required even if direct ad spend is lower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press coverage as earned media
rubrics_metrics.description: Press coverage includes feature articles, news discussions, and mentions by niche bloggers — all forms of earned media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices to get press coverage include releasing regular press releases to targeted media outlets and developing relationships with bloggers and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media mentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any organic mention of your brand on social media counts as earned media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is relatively easy to generate but can be positive or negative; use social media management tools to monitor trends and respond quickly. Publish high-quality thought leadership and share it to encourage organic mentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influencer partnerships (earned via relationship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although influencer partnerships are often paid, they can function as earned media when influencers share your brand positively through relationship-building or unpaid recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand who your audience follows, build relationships, send samples or mention influencers on your channels to encourage authentic, unpaid mentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews and testimonials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews on platforms like Google, Yelp, product-specific sites, and user-generated content (e.g., unboxing videos) are forms of earned media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage review strategy proactively to encourage positive reviews and mitigate negative ones; monitor review sites and consider incentives carefully to drive favorable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set clear goals for earned media
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with specific objectives so you can evaluate campaign success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals might include boosting overall awareness, reaching a new demographic, increasing positive product reviews, or improving search engine rankings — choose metrics aligned to these goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build an earned media strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan who you need to reach and how to influence what they think about your brand or product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess current perceptions, media consumption habits, locations, and concerns of the target audience; identify channels and influencers to target as part of the strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell your story to encourage pickup
rubrics_metrics.description: While third parties ultimately produce earned media, brands can seed stories and start conversations to increase pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly post on social media, publish press releases, contact influencers/journalists/bloggers, offer samples or incentives, and create unique, compelling content to motivate organic coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote and engage post-publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Earned media efforts continue after coverage appears; brands must promote content and engage with audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use all channels to amplify coverage, thank customers for positive feedback, respond constructively to negative feedback, and maintain ongoing conversations where customers are active.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Earned media outcomes vary in timing and often require sustained effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing credibility and entering new markets can take months; consistently deliver engaging content to the right audience rather than expecting immediate viral results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs are traditional earned media measurements that show impact on media channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track reach and impressions (exposure and audience demographics) and share of voice (compare your brand’s presence to competitors across channels) using analytics platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes assess the audience’s response to earned media and whether they care about your message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track engagement (clicks, likes, shares, comments) and brand sentiment by monitoring mentions and context; use sentiment-analysis tools (e.g., Cision’s Stance) to understand tone and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure business results
rubrics_metrics.description: Connect earned media to bottom-line metrics to demonstrate impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute conversions (purchases, demo signups, downloads, page visits, loyalty program joins) to earned coverage and calculate ROI to show value to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and manage negative earned media
rubrics_metrics.description: Earned media exposure can be negative as well as positive, so monitoring and mitigation are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social listening and earned media tools to detect negative mentions early, respond appropriately, and incorporate reputation management into your earned media strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in earned media tools and attribution technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern earned media analysis technology evaluates outputs, outcomes, and business results and can attribute customer actions to coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specialized measurement and PR analytics tools to move beyond flawed metrics (like AVE) and directly link coverage to lead generation and sales where possible.
